outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms a CUA is required, file a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning, including a project description, site plan, floor plan, elevation drawings, and a good-neighbor operating plan. What to say: Frame the application as an enlargement of an existing restaurant use that has been on the site since at least 1998, with Planning approvals in 2018 and 2019, and an active Type 47 license since October 2019. Commit to operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place with meals prepared and served on the premises and alcohol service subordinate to food. Commit to the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD § 249.60(d) requirements: outside lighting, window signage limited to 33%, and 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades. Propose conditioned hours for the outdoor area (e.g., 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.) and commit to seated-only outdoor seating with alcohol dispensed only inside or by wait staff at the patron's seat. Commit to sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, noise and odor controls, garbage containment inside, and appointment of a community liaison. Note that the restaurant is separate fro…

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit application with the San Francisco Entertainment Commission, depending on whether entertainment is a primary use or runs until 2 a.m. (POE) or is a secondary use ending by 10 or 11 p.m. (LLP). What to say: State that the restaurant proposes live entertainment with amplified sound as an accessory use to the existing restaurant, with performers ending by [state the hour]. Commit to the hours, noise controls, and capacity limits the Commission requires. Note that the restaurant has operated at this address since at least 1998 and holds an active Type 47 license. If seeking a POE, note that zoning permits Nighttime Entertainment on the first story in NCT-Mission without a zoning hearing (§ 754), but the Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on the POE application. If seeking an LLP, note that nearby restaurants with LLPs (at 2327 Mission St and 2293 Mission St) were approved as accessory uses in 10–24 days.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application with the San Francisco Department of Building Inspection for tenant improvements to construct the outdoor seating area, including any grading, lighting, fencing, and ADA access. What to say: Submit scaled drawings of the outdoor seating layout, showing the number of seats, the path of travel, ADA-compliant access, lighting, and any structures (e.g., fencing, shade structures). Note that the building permit will be routed to Planning for zoning review per Planning Code § 175(a), and that the zoning review will be satisfied by the Conditional Use Authorization (if one is required) or by Planning's confirmation that the outdoor area meets § 202.2(a)(7) limits. If a change of occupancy occurs (from Group B to Assembly Group A-2 or vice versa), the plans must show compliance with the Building Code for the new occupancy group.
outcomes.note: The records confirm a building permit is needed for tenant improvements but do not state the specific code sections, routing to Planning, drawing requirements, or occupancy group classifications mentioned.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After DPH plan check approval and after the building permit is issued, schedule a pre-opening inspection with DPH and a final building inspection with DBI. What to say: Contact the DPH plan reviewer assigned to the project at least two weeks in advance to schedule the pre-opening inspection at about 80% completion of the outdoor seating construction, and again for the final inspection before opening. Contact DBI to schedule the final building inspection after the outdoor seating is complete. Both inspections must pass before the outdoor seating can be used by the public.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: These are day and cost ranges for the approvals in the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Entertainment Commission permit, and Health permit to operate), assuming they are granted. The range is 4–10 months to approval and $3,100–$15,000 in government fees. The Conditional Use Authorization is the critical path: a CUA filing without construction typically costs $2,747 on the 2023–24 schedule (adjusted to about $3,150 by early 2023) and takes 120–300 days including pre-application meetings, environmental review, neighborhood notification, Planning Commission hearing, and a 30-day appeal period. The one outdoor seating CUA nearby (2323 Mission St) took 268 days from filing to approval in 2017. The Entertainment Commission permit (Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance) adds $612–$2,708 (2026–27 fees; earlier fees were lower) and 30–120 days for intake, referrals, posted notice, and a Commission hearing. The health permit to operate costs $470 (application) and takes 14–45 days after plan check approval for the pre-opening inspection. If Planning confirms the outdoor seating can be approved administratively under § 202.2(a)(7) without a CUA, the timeline drops to 45–120 days (for the Entertainment Commission permit and health inspection) and the cost drops to about $1,000–$3,000. This estimate does not include building permit fees (which depend on construction valuation), architect and expediter fees, or time to a denial or withdrawal. It also does not include the time or cost to obtain ABC approval of the premises modification or to amend the Type 47 license conditions, which may be required if ABC considers the outdoor seating a change to the licensed premises. Confirm the CUA requirement and the SUD expansion rule applicability with San Francisco Planning before filing.
